Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroGreen Energy Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AeroGreen Energy Inc.'s results for the Q3. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Development Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AeroGreen Energy Inc. had a strong Q3, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements. First, our operating capacity reached 6,250 MW with generation output of 4,850 GWh, showing robust growth. Second, significant market trends like plummeting solar costs and storage surges are propelling us forward. Third, construction progress across our projects remains on track with key CODs approaching. Fourth, our debt levels are well-managed at conservative ratios with improving financing costs. Fifth, PPA pricing is stabilizing higher while we secure valuable contract extensions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance and expand on several of these.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue reached $1.2 billion, representing a 28% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 32%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $350 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $280 million, or $1.75 per share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Before diving deeper into the numbers, let me provide context on the core operational metrics that underpin these results: our operating capacity in megawatts and generation output in gigawatt-hours. These are the lifeblood of our business as a leading pure-play renewable energy developer and operator, with a diversified portfolio spanning utility-scale solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, and energy storage systems. Our focus on high-quality assets in prime resource regimes continues to drive industry-leading returns, even amidst a volatile merchant market influenced by curtailment pressures in ERCOT and negative pricing episodes in Europe.

As of September 30, 2024, our total operating capacity stood at 6,250 MW, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from 4,875 MW at the end of Q3 2023. This growth was propelled by 1,050 MW of new capacity additions during the quarter, including the full commercialization of our 450 MW SunForge Solar project in California's Imperial Valley and the 350 MW Phase II expansion of the Gale Force onshore wind farm in Texas' panhandle. Quarter-over-quarter, capacity grew 8% from 5,775 MW in Q2, reflecting minimal unplanned outages—our fleet availability hit 98.7%, above our 97% target.

Turning to generation output, we delivered 4,850 GWh in Q3 2024, up 22% year-over-year from 3,975 GWh in the prior-year period and 12% quarter-over-quarter from 4,325 GWh. This outperformance versus capacity growth stems from a blended fleet capacity factor of 34.2%, a 210 basis points improvement year-over-year, driven by favorable wind regimes and our aggressive repowering initiatives. For context, this equates to powering approximately 1.1 million U.S. households for the quarter, based on EIA average consumption data, while avoiding 3.2 million metric tons of CO2 emissions—progress toward our net-zero operations goal by 2035.

Let's break this down by technology segment, as our portfolio diversification mitigates weather and resource variability—a key strategic edge in clean tech.

Solar PV, at 3,450 MW operating capacity or 55% of total, grew 35% year-over-year, with Q3 additions including the 450 MW SunForge project, which utilizes high-efficiency bifacial TOPCon modules from First Solar and Longi—achieving a DC/AC ratio of 1.4:1 for enhanced low-light performance. Generation reached 1,925 GWh, up 30% year-over-year, with a capacity factor of 25.8% (up 150 basis points). This uplift reflects our pivot to tracker-optimized designs from Nextracker, which boosted energy yield by 8-12% in dusty Southwest sites, and our integration of 150 MW-hours of behind-the-meter ESS for clipping recapture. Regionally, our U.S. Southwest assets (60% of solar capacity) benefited from above-normal insolation—1,050 kWh/kWp annually—while our 400 MW Australian portfolio navigated softer output due to cooler monsoon conditions, offset by AUD/USD tailwinds in merchant sales.

Wind, at 2,300 MW operating capacity or 37% of total, expanded 22% year-over-year, highlighted by the 350 MW Gale Force Phase II, featuring Vestas V150-6.0 MW turbines with 15% larger rotors for superior annual energy production in low-wind-speed sites. Our offshore segment—250 MW from the Atlantic Breeze floating project off New Jersey—ramped to full operations post-FID in Q1. Total wind generation hit 2,650 GWh, a 26% year-over-year surge, with a standout 42.1% capacity factor (up 320 basis points), fueled by stronger-than-expected shear in the U.S. Great Plains and North Sea equivalents. We've repowered 180 MW of legacy assets with Siemens Gamesa SG 14.0-222 DD turbines, unlocking 15-20% yield gains through taller hubs and longer blades. U.S. assets (75% of wind) thrived under IRA PTC adders averaging $25/MWh, while European curtailment in Spain capped output at 92% of P50 forecasts.

Energy storage, at 500 MW / 1,200 MWh operating capacity or 8% of total, doubled year-over-year, anchored by the 200 MW/800 MWh Ironclad battery in ERCOT, deployed with Tesla Megapacks for 4-hour duration and 90% round-trip efficiency. While not directly contributing to GWh generation, it enabled 350 GWh of firming services, arbitraging intra-day spreads up to $150/MWh during heatwaves. Capacity factor equivalent for dispatchable output was 75%, reflecting our AI-driven Oasis software for predictive bidding in CAISO and PJM markets.

Regionally: U.S. (75% of capacity, 4,000 MW) delivered 3,450 GWh (71% of total output), boosted by IRA incentives—our effective PTC/ITC yield now exceeds 50% on new builds. Texas and California represented 45% of additions, though grid queue delays pushed two 300 MW solar projects to Q1 2025. Europe (15%, 950 MW): 825 GWh output, tempered by REPowerEU-driven congestion in Iberia, where we've secured 80% offtake via CfDs with Iberdrola at €55/MWh. Asia-Pacific/LatAm (10%, 300 MW): 575 GWh, with Chile's Atacama solar shining at 32% capacity factor amid copper demand surge.

Key trends and technical initiatives driving performance: We've seen a sector-wide capacity factor convergence toward 35-40% blended, per IRENA data, as bifacial solar efficiencies hit 23% module-level (vs. 20% in 2022) and wind rotor diameters scale to 250m+. Our "YieldMax" program—$250 million capex in 2024—includes AI wake steering on 40% of wind farms (partnered with WindESCo), delivering 5-7% AEP uplift, and perovskite tandem cell pilots on 50 MW, targeting 30%+ efficiency by 2026. Weather was a tailwind: U.S. wind speeds 10% above NREL normals, solar GHI +5% per NSRDB. However, Q3 hurricanes caused 2% downtime in Gulf Coast assets, mitigated by our $50 million resilience fund for elevated nacelles and flood-proof inverters.

Operationally, we're positioned for 15-20% annual capacity CAGR through 2027, with 12 GW in late-stage construction—including 2 GW offshore wind leveraging U.S. BOEM lease rounds—and 25 GW in the pipeline. We're shifting 30% of new builds to hybrid solar+wind+storage parks, like our 800 MW Mojave Nexus project, to capture hybrid PPAs at $40-50/MWh fixed, insulating against merchant volatility seen in Australia's NEM negative pricing. Battery co-location has de-risked 60% of our U.S. portfolio, enabling value stacking via ancillary services (15% of EBITDA). Margins expanded to 82% gross on generation (up 300 basis points year-over-year) due to O&M optimization—leveraging Orbia's drone-based PV cleaning, cutting soiling losses to <2%.

Looking ahead, Q4 capacity will hit 6,800 MW with 550 MW online, targeting 5,200 GWh output at 35% capacity factor. Full-year 2024 guidance: 18,500 GWh generation (20% growth) and EBITDA of $1.2-1.3 billion.

To further contextualize, let's discuss the significant market trends shaping our results. We're at an inflection point where policy tailwinds, technological advancements, and supply-demand dynamics are accelerating the global energy transition. According to the latest IEA World Energy Outlook, global renewable capacity additions hit 525 GW in 2023—up 50% year-over-year—and we're on track for over 600 GW in 2024. Solar PV alone accounted for 75% of that, with 390 GW deployed, driven by module prices plummeting 42% year-over-year to an average of $0.22 per watt for Tier 1 bifacial PERC and TOPCon panels. This cost deflation—fueled by China's hyperscale manufacturing capacity, now at 1.2 TW annually—has driven the global LCOE for utility-scale solar down to $24/MWh in optimal markets, undercutting new fossil fuel builds by 20-30%. Wind followed closely, with onshore additions up 15% to 115 GW, though offshore wind faced headwinds from permitting delays and supply chain bottlenecks, capping growth at 25 GW.

Energy storage is the real game-changer, with utility-scale battery deployments surging 60% to 75 GW/190 GWh globally, with pack-level costs dipping below $130/kWh for LFP chemistries—thanks to innovations like CATL's condensed battery tech and Tesla's Megapack scaling. This has unlocked hybrid solar-plus-storage projects, where we're seeing IRRs north of 12-15% even in conservative financing scenarios. Green hydrogen is gaining traction too, with electrolyzer capex falling 25% to $450/kW, positioning it for cost-competitive dispatchable power by 2027, per BloombergNEF forecasts.

In the U.S., the Inflation Reduction Act continues to supercharge demand—tax credits under Sections 45X and 48E have unlocked $100 billion+ in manufacturing investments, with solar and storage module production ramping to 200 GW domestic capacity by 2025. Our U.S. project pipeline grew 35% quarter-over-quarter to 12 GWdc, anchored by long-duration PPAs with hyperscalers like Google and Microsoft, who signed 25 GW of corporate renewables in Q3 alone. Corporate PPAs now represent 40% of U.S. additions, with pricing holding firm at $25-35/MWh due to REC multipliers.

Europe's REPowerEU plan is delivering: despite permitting bottlenecks, the region added 55 GW of renewables in 2023, with Germany and Spain leading at 15 GW and 12 GW respectively. The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is pressuring imports, boosting local content rules and favoring our European EPC operations. Margins here are expanding 200-300 basis points on higher AD/CVD-protected module pricing.

In Asia-Pacific, China's dominance in the supply chain—controlling 95% of polysilicon and 80% of cells—has created both opportunities and risks. While wafer prices hit historic lows, we're mitigating downside through our offtake agreements with LONGi and JinkoSolar, securing 5 GW at $0.20/W fixed. India's PLI scheme is exploding, with 20 GW of domestic manufacturing online, feeding a 50 GW annual solar tender pipeline.

These trends directly impacted our P&L: 65% of revenue from development and EPC of solar-storage hybrids—our SolaraHybrid platform secured three 500 MW deals in the U.S. Southwest at blended PPAs of $32/MWh. Our contracted backlog stands at $18 billion across 25 GW, up 40% year-over-year. Strategically, we've allocated $500 million of capex to vertical integration, including a 2 GW TOPCon cell fab in Texas qualifying for full IRA domestic content bonuses—targeting 25% module margins by H2 2025. In storage, our JV with Fluence has deployed 1.5 GWh year-to-date. On hydrogen, we're piloting a 100 MW PEM electrolyzer project in California. Risks include interconnection queues exceeding 2 TW in the U.S. and potential tariffs, but our 80% fixed-price contracts and $5 billion liquidity provide resilience. Renewables are now the cheapest new-build electricity source globally, with clean tech capex set to hit $2 trillion annually by 2030, supporting our 25-30% CAGR.

On our balance sheet, let's focus on debt levels and financing costs, a cornerstone in this capital-intensive sector. As of September 30, our total gross debt stood at $5.2 billion, down 8% year-over-year from $5.65 billion, reflecting strong free cash flow generation of $450 million in the first nine months—driven by 95% contracted revenues from long-duration PPAs and merchant tail optimization in ERCOT and CAISO markets. Net debt, after subtracting our $1.1 billion cash pile bolstered by IRA transferability proceeds, came in at $4.1 billion, yielding a conservative net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 2.8x—well below our 3.5x target and in line with peers.

Composition: 65% or $3.4 billion is non-recourse project-level financing, primarily construction and term loans tied to our 1.2 GW solar-plus-storage pipeline, backed by robust DSCRs averaging 1.6x pro forma for recent projects like SunForge. The remaining 35%, or $1.8 billion, is corporate revolver and senior notes, with our $750 million revolving credit facility undrawn and maturing in 2027—giving $1.2 billion liquidity headroom.

Maturities are well-laddered: only 12% or $624 million rolls off in the next 12 months, with an average debt maturity of 6.2 years. We've extended $1.1 billion of near-term project debt this quarter, locking in blended rates ahead of Fed cuts.

Financing costs improved to a weighted average of 4.2% from 4.6% a year ago, a 40 basis points compression. This includes a $500 million green bond issuance in Q2 at 3.9% coupon—10-year fixed, certified under ICMA Green Bond Principles. We've tapped $1.8 billion in green and sustainability-linked financing since 2022, shaving ~50 basis points off costs.

In the U.S. (70% of portfolio), IRA ITCs/PTCs supercharged deals like our 300 MW BESS securing a $400 million tax equity partnership at under 3.5% effective after-tax cost. Europe (20%) saw 4.8% rates, mitigated by €300 million EIB loans. Asia-Pacific (10%) at 5.1%, hedged via swaps.

We're ahead with deleveraging from O&M efficiencies (down 15% via AI) and hedging 70% variable rates. Expect net debt-to-EBITDA to 2.5x by year-end 2025 as $800 million FCF funds growth, with $2.5 billion capex 60% project-financed at sub-4%.

Now, I'll pass the call to Mike Chen to discuss our project development pipeline.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Elena. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 25 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Our Clean Tech platform is firing on all cylinders with over 4.2 GW in active construction or late-stage development as of quarter-end. We're tracking 98% on-budget, thanks to EPC partnerships with Bechtel and Fluor, who've internalized lessons from past supply chain disruptions. Inflation in steel and modules has moderated—polysilicon spot prices down 35% year-to-date to $8/kg—allowing fixed-price contracts protecting margins at 18-22% unlevered IRR.

Solar fleet (55% of queue at 2.3 GWdc): Desert Peak Solar in Arizona—650 MWdc single-axis tracker with LONGi Hi-MO 6 bifacial modules at 23.5% efficiency. Foundations 100% complete, 92% modules on-site, 78% overall progress, accelerated 3 months by Array Technologies' DuraTrack HZ v3. Mechanical completion Q4 2024, full COD year-end, under 15-year PPA with APS at $28/MWh. Coastal Rise Solar + Storage Hybrid (400 MWdc + 200 MW/400 MWh BESS) at 65% complete; COD Q1 2025 due to PG&E upgrades, capturing $150/kW ITC adder. In APAC, 300 MWdc in India's Rajasthan at 45% EPC, COD H1 2025 at INR 2.4/kWh.

Offshore wind (25% at 1 GW): Horizon Winds East off New Jersey—600 MW with Vestas V236-15.0 MW turbines. Monopile installation 52% done, first power Q3 2026, full COD H2 2026 at $65/MWh LCOE. UK North Sea Gale Force (400 MW) at 28% post-FID.

Battery storage and hybrids (15% at 450 MW/900 MWh): Lone Star BESS (300 MW/1,200 MWh) in ERCOT at 88%, COD August 2024. Australian flow battery pilot at 72%, COD Q4 2024.

Emerging tech: ElectroLynx H2 (50 MW electrolyzer) at 22% civils, COD H1 2026 at $2.50/kg.

Portfolio-wide, 12% quarter-over-quarter construction velocity uptick from AI digital twins. Backlog 8.5 GW contracted, capex $1.8 billion of $2.4 billion budgeted. Expect 1.5 GW CODs H2 2024, 2.8 GW in 2025.

Next, Lisa Patel will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Mike. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. This quarter's operations avoided 3.2 million metric tons of CO2, advancing our net-zero by 2035 goal. We're enhancing fleet resilience with investments in elevated structures and flood-proofing, while AI optimizations cut soiling and downtime. We are also actively involved in community engagement, supporting local initiatives around our projects, and prioritizing ESG in financing—35% green-linked debt. These efforts benefit the environment and create long-term stakeholder value, aligning with trends like CBAM and corporate Scope 2 demands.

I'll now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Lisa. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter, highlighted by operational excellence, market tailwinds, project momentum, financial discipline, and commercial strength. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Green Horizon Capital. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez:
Thanks, and good morning team. Strong quarter on the project front—congrats on the backlog growth. Could you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Mike Chen:
Thanks, John. As I mentioned, supply chain has improved markedly, but we've navigated past bottlenecks effectively. Inflation moderation and fixed-price contracts keep us 98% on-budget. For instance, module deliveries for Desert Peak are 92% on-site despite global order books, thanks to diversified suppliers like LONGi. Grid queues remain a watchpoint—Coastal Rise slipped slightly due to PG&E—but FERC reforms help. Overall, no major delays; we're accelerating with modular tech, on track for 1.5 GW CODs this half. Hurricanes caused minor Gulf downtime, but our resilience fund mitigates. Happy to provide more project specifics.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Green Horizon Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, and good morning team. What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Sarah. Emerging markets like India, Chile, and Southeast Asia represent 10% of our capacity today but key growth vectors, with 20 GW pipeline entry via PLI schemes and copper demand. We're leveraging local manufacturing to avoid tariffs—e.g., Rajasthan project COD H1 2025. In APAC/LatAm, hybrids de-risk grids, with Vietnam floating solar pilots. Strategy: JV partnerships like Fluence for storage, offtake secures (SECI auctions at $30/MWh), and ESG premiums for hyperscalers. IRA domestic focus keeps U.S. core (75%), but emerging adds diversification, targeting 20% portfolio share by 2027 with 12-15% IRRs.

On a related note, PPA trends support this: New solar at $28-32/MWh, hybrids $42/MWh premium. We've executed 15 GW PPAs/extensions last 24 months, 85% contracted. Pricing stabilized post-2022 lows—up 25-35% from $21/MWh—due to inflation, now firming with escalators. U.S. C&I at $25-35/MWh, Europe €45/MWh post-crisis, India $30/MWh. Extensions on legacy: 1.2 GW YTD, like Desert Sun repower at $48/MWh vs. original $55/MWh, low capex $0.45/W. Merchant tail 10-20%, ESG-linked 20% of deals at 5-8% premiums. Q4 2 GW at $30-35/MWh; extensions add 1 GW. Positions us for 12-15% EBITDA CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with EcoInvest Partners. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, David. Competition is intensifying with 600 GW global adds projected, but our edges—diversified high-quality assets, 90% locked offtake, vertical integration like our Texas cell fab—set us apart. We differentiate via hybrids (30% new builds), YieldMax AI yields (5-7% uplift), and fortress balance sheet (2.8x leverage). Peers face higher leverage; our O&M cuts (15%) and 82% generation margins lead. Policy like IRA/REPowerEU favors us; we're shaping markets with pilots in H2/perovskites. Confident in outpacing via execution.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of AeroGreen Energy Inc. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
